content: OAuth CSRF protection requires a server-generated random, unpredictable state value stored server-side (signed cookie or session) before redirecting to Google, then validated on callback that the returned state matches and has not expired (e.g. 10 minute window) and is single-use (deleted/invalidated after one use to prevent replay). Session fixation prevention requires regenerating the session identifier/creating a brand-new session after successful authentication rather than reusing a pre-auth session id. For multi-instance deployments, state/session storage needs to be shared (Redis or DB-backed), not in-memory per-server-instance.
